chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whatever you are uncertain about regarding what has already passed, then complete it as it is."

key_terms.كَمَا هُوَ: As it is/in its current state

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one is uncertain about a previously completed act of worship?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the principle of 'istishab al-asl' (presumption of continuity) within the jurisprudence of doubt, specifically addressing cases where uncertainty arises regarding acts already completed. It reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that in the absence of definitive proof to the contrary, the original state of validity is maintained, preventing unnecessary burden (gharar) on the believer. This ruling is foundational in the chapter of 'Ahkam al-Sahw' (Rulings of Forgetfulness/Doubt), emphasizing stability in religious practice.
